context: Grandpa tells Sho an old tale, using archaic speech.
purpose: WIDENED SCENARIO: elder storytelling; archaic negation and old register spoken naturally.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、昔の話して!
lines.en: Grandpa, tell me an old story!
lines.style: eager small child voice, bright warm excited bouncing delivery throughout

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: 以前、この村には橋が無かった。
lines.en: Long ago, this village had no bridge.
lines.style: gravelly old man voice, soft warm slow nostalgic delivery throughout

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: えっ、川はどう渡ったの?
lines.en: Huh, how did they cross the river?
lines.style: surprised small child voice, bright warm wide-eyed delivery throughout

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: 誰も渡れぬ日も、あったものよ。
lines.en: There were days no one could cross.
lines.style: gravelly old man voice, soft warm slow nostalgic delivery throughout

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ほかに、道は無かったの?
lines.style: curious small child voice, bright warm earnest delivery throughout

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: ほかの道は、あまり無かったのじゃ。
lines.style: gravelly old man voice, soft warm slow nostalgic delivery throughout

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: sympathetic small child voice, bright warm gentle delivery throughout

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: 皆で力を合わせ、橋を作ったのじゃ。
lines.en: Everyone joined forces and built a bridge.
lines.style: gravelly old man voice, soft warm proud nostalgic delivery throughout

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: すごい!以前の人は強いね。
lines.en: Amazing! People back then were strong.
lines.style: impressed small child voice, bright warm admiring delivery throughout
